description: DevSpace - The Fastest Developer Tool for Kubernetes ⚡ Automate your deployment workflow with DevSpace and develop software directly inside Kubernetes.

summary.one_liner: DevSpace is a client-only CLI tool for building, deploying, hot-reloading and debugging cloud-native applications directly inside Kubernetes clusters.
summary.what_it_does: DevSpace runs as a single binary CLI on your machine and talks directly to a Kubernetes cluster using your existing kube-context, with no server-side component. Workflows (image building, deployment, dependencies) are declared in a devspace.yaml file that can be versioned with code and shared across a team. It provides bi-directional file synchronization between local files and running containers, so code edits show up in the container without rebuilding images. It can build multiple images in parallel, tag them automatically, and deploy an application with one command. It also automates port-forwarding and log streaming, and supports opening container terminals and connecting debuggers. The README says it has been tested with local clusters (minikube, k3s, MicroK8s, kind) and managed clusters (GKE, EKS, AKS, DigitalOcean).
use_cases: Hot reload code changes inside a running Kubernetes container
Deploy a microservice project with a single command
Share standardized deployment workflows across a dev team
Automate image building and tagging in parallel
Automatic port-forwarding and log streaming for Kubernetes pods
Debug applications running in a remote or local cluster
how_to_run: Install the devspace CLI binary (see the README's quickstart/getting started guide)
Create or check out a project containing a devspace.yaml file
Point your kube-context at a local or remote Kubernetes cluster
Run `devspace deploy` to build and deploy the project
Run DevSpace development commands from the terminal inside your IDE to sync files and stream logs
notable: Single declarative devspace.yaml file stores build and deploy workflows alongside code
Bi-directional file sync for hot reloading without rebuilding images
No server-side component; uses kubectl-style kube-context directly
CNCF sandbox project originally created by Loft Labs
caveats: Requires access to a Kubernetes cluster (local or remote); the README says it cannot be used without one
Contributing instructions reference an old Go requirement (1.11.4+) and vendored modules, which may be outdated
README gives little install detail; points to external getting-started docs
keywords: run app in cluster from ide
